title: A note on existentially t-henselian fields
summary: A field is existentially t-henselian if it is has the same existential theory in the first-order language of rings as a field that admits a nontrivial henselian valuation. This property turns out to be equivalent to $\mathbb{Z}$-largeness, which is a property identified in previous work with Fehm, and which holds for $F$ if and only if $tF[\![t]\!]$ is not Diophantine in $F(\!(t)\!)$, without extra constants.
